turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hi there, how are you feeling today?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Ugh, the twins want separate parties this year.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's a big ask at their age. Are you open to two parties, or would one party with two cakes keep the peace?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Hang on, I'm going to chat with my friend for a bit. Just wait until I say I'm back.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Sam, do you know the wifi password here? My phone keeps dropping off.

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: It's on the back of the router, I think. The long one with all the letters.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Ugh, I typed that in twice already.

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Did you try forgetting the network and joining again? That fixed mine last week.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: No, I'll try that now. Hold on.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Sure thing. So, are you giving in to separate parties, or holding out for a shared one?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: One party, two cakes. I don't have the energy for two.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Fair enough. Let each twin pick half the games so nobody feels left out.
